History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
Adult female with asthma and known peanut allergy developed rapidly progressive upper-lip swelling, dyspnea, chest tightness, and dizziness ~30 min after eating prawn soup; clinician suspected anaphylaxis, instructed immediate antihistamine use, and arranged emergency transfer to hospital.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden swelling of upper lip after ingestion of prawn soup.  
• Timeline:
  – ~19:00 today – Patient ate prawn soup (first time trying this item).  
  – Within ~30 min – Noticed tingling then swelling at left corner of upper lip, progressed to entire upper lip.  
  – Progressive worsening since onset; feels “really pumping” and enlarging.  
• Associated symptoms: Difficulty breathing (“can’t breathe that well”), possible chest tightness, dizziness.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None tried before consult.  
• Previous similar episodes:
  – 1 year ago: Woke with facial swelling and breathing difficulty after late-night Chinese meal; self-treated with Salbutamol inhaler only.  
  – Age 6: Required hospital treatment (details unknown) for severe allergic reaction to peanuts.  
• System review (limited to what was discussed):
  – Respiratory: Dyspnea present.  
  – Cardiovascular: Dizziness; no syncope reported.  
  – GI, GU, neuro, derm, other systems: Not discussed.  
  – Pertinent negatives: No explicit mention of rash or abdominal pain.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – uses Salbutamol inhaler PRN; no preventative “brown” inhaler.  
• Peanut allergy – prior severe reaction requiring hospital treatment in childhood.  
• No other chronic conditions recorded.

Medications:
• Salbutamol inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Intermittent antihistamines for allergies – specific agent/dose not documented.

Allergies:
• Peanuts – anaphylaxis history.  
• Shellfish (prawn) – suspected new allergy; not previously confirmed.

Social History:
• Lives with mother (present during call).  
• No current smoker/alcohol/substance history documented; notes occasional alcohol use in past (“quite drunk” during prior episode).  
• Recently dining out with friends.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed via teleconsult; no vitals obtained.)

Investigations:
• None obtained during virtual consult.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected anaphylaxis to shellfish (prawn)
  – Progressive lip swelling, dyspnea, dizziness shortly after exposure.  
  – Plan:
    • Instructed immediate oral antihistamine (available at home).  
    • Advised companion to call emergency services (999) for urgent transport.  
    • Will require emergency department evaluation, possible intramuscular epinephrine, airway support, observation.

Issue 2: Long-term allergy management
  – History of severe allergy to peanuts and probable shellfish.  
  – Plan (post-hospital discharge):
    • Arrange follow-up visit to review reaction details.  
    • Prescribe epinephrine auto-injector(s); educate on use.  
    • Refer to allergy specialist for confirmatory testing and comprehensive action plan.  
    • Discuss carrying antihistamines and emergency ID bracelet.

Issue 3: Asthma
  – Known asthma; currently uses rescue inhaler only.  
  – Plan (at follow-up):
    • Reassess asthma control; consider adding preventer inhaler if indicated.  
    • Provide asthma action plan.

General Plan items:
• Encourage avoidance of known allergens; provide dietary counseling.  
• Document allergies prominently in her medical record.

Quality checks:

– Missing expected elements: vitals, full medication list (name/dose/frequency), full allergy list confirmation, past surgical history, family/social/obstetric history.  
– Internal conflicts: None noted.  
– Transcript quality: Clear dialogue; no significant inaudible sections, but limited objective data due to virtual nature.
